newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S CONCORDE TO LAUNCH OPEN-ENDED FUND.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S CONCORDE TO LAUNCH OPEN-ENDED FUND.

text.p: Hungary's Concorde Investment Fund Management Company is to launch its second fund, to be called Concorde 2000, an open ended fund, Concorde officials told a news conference on Tuesday.

"We plan to keep a diversified portfolio and will invest on the long-term," Laszlo Szabo, managing director of the fund manager said. "We will sell any share if basic changes occur in the fundamental assessment," he said.

The fund will issue at least 800 units of series "A" investment notes and at least 200 and a maximum 10,000 units of series "B" registered notes, all with 100,000 forints face value. Series "B" notes will be available also to foreigners.
The issue price will be face value and subscriptions will run from August 18 to 22.

Concorde said in the issue prospectus that on average at least 35 to 40 percent of the capital would be invested in shares. This proportion may rise to up to 85 percent in favourable market conditions, and may fall to zero in a pessimistic scenario.
Concorde Investment Fund Management Company is the wholly owned unit of Concorde Securities.
